Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-05 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Sofia Patel (Aurum Head of ML), Marcus Lin (Infra), Dr. Elena Ruiz (CTO), Rajesh Nair (Security)

Summary (auto):
Quick intake on dedicated reserved GPUs for Aurum Bio's inference workloads. Focus: support rapid burst up to ~600 RPS for embeddings and nlp-chat, isolation requirements for PHI-ish data, VPC/private deployment constraints, and security/compliance (KMS, audit). Agreed to run perf checks and exchange traffic traces; Redwood to propose a reserved capacity configuration and pricing.

Topics:
- Current infra and model types
- Bursting patterns and warm-pool strategy
- Isolation and VPC connectivity vs Hosted fallback
- Security: KMS, audit logs, SOC2/ISO
- Next steps: perf test + pricing + pilot kickoff

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on a friday, appreciate it. I'll hand off to Liam for the deep bits but quick intros — I'm Maya, AE on the PNW team.
[00:08] Sofia Patel: Hi, Sofia here, Head of ML at Aurum Bio. Short on time today, so we want the rapid path.
[00:12] Marcus Lin: Marcus, infra, I'll be implementing.
[00:15] Liam O'Connor: Hey all, Liam from Redwood, systems SE. Nice to meet you.
[00:20] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Elena, CTO. We'll probably ask the hard questions.
[00:24] Rajesh Nair: Rajesh, security — mostly compliance and key mgmt.

[02:10] Maya Chen: Goal for today is to understand your traffic and isolation needs so we can recommend either Hosted, Dedicated, or a Private anchored deployment. big picture — Sofia, can you run us through what you're serving today?
[02:22] Sofia Patel: Sure; we run a mix: small chat assistants inside our R&D portal (low latency, p95 ~200-300ms target), and large embedding jobs for similarity search used for biomedical retrieval. The embeddings are bursty — nightly batches but also on-demand during experiments where we see spikes to several hundred reqs per minute, occasionally into high hundreds. We're thinking of reserved GPUs because cost and predictability matter.
[02:42] Liam O'Connor: Helpful. Do you have rough token sizes / sequence lengths? embeddings are about 1k tokens total including prompt?
[02:48] Sofia Patel: Embeddings are short — payload small, but scale: each embedding call processes between 512 and 2048 tokens depending on chunking. Chat flows vary, avg 256 tokens.

[05:05] Marcus Lin: Our infra today: k8s cluster on GCP with private VPC, we use Cloud VPN to some research labs. We cannot send PHI to public hosted endpoints without anonymization; that's a hard constraint.
[05:20] Rajesh Nair: Correct — anything with patient identifiers needs to stay within our VPC or be encrypted with customer-managed keys. SOC2 is table stakes; we also want evidence for encryption at rest and audit trails.

[06:55] Liam O'Connor: Understood. So two important axes: isolation/throughput. Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) gives you the isolation you need — dedicated tenancy and optional VPC peering for Redwood Private. For Hosted, we can do VPC egress but that may not satisfy strict PHI mandates.
[07:12] Sofia Patel: Can you quantify prewarm time? when a sudden spike hits, how do you keep p95 low without paying for idle GPUs all day?
[07:25] Liam O'Connor: Great question. We use warm pools and prewarming; there's a tradeoff. Typical prewarm for a warm pool is ~90-180 seconds to reach steady LLM throughput depending on model size. For really sudden spikes we recommend a small hot pool plus autoscaled reserved nodes that can burst into a shared overflow pool — Redwood's burst strategy supports automatic fallback to compatible quantized variants if exact hardware's busy. That said, we're careful with cold-starts; if you need <1s p95 for cold, you'll need more headroom.

[09:40] Dr. Elena Ruiz: What's the failover? If our dedicated pool is saturated, do calls fail or do they route to hosted? We have regulatory limits on data leaving the VPC.
[09:53] Maya Chen: Configurable policy. Common pattern: canary/burst fallback to a private hosted tier that is still within a dedicated VPC boundary, or we can route to a model variant that runs on cheaper quantized infra but within the same private deployment. For PHI, we recommend never routing to public hosted endpoints — instead Redwood Private or Dedicated with strict tenancy.

[11:30] Rajesh Nair: KMS — we use cloud KMS and an HSM for certain keys. We need key control and audit logs for any model artifacts and request logs. Is that supported?
[11:45] Liam O'Connor: Yes — for Private and Dedicated we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM, and Redwood emits audit logs for token-level usage and request traces. There are some names sometimes mismatched in automated logs — the transcript might show "KV cash" in our exports ha — but the system supports structured audit records you can ship to your SIEM.

[13:15] Marcus Lin: Latency targets: we want p95 chat <250ms and embeddings bulk throughput of ~10k embeddings/hr sustained, peaks up to 40k/hr in short windows. How many GPUs do you think?
[13:34] Liam O'Connor: Rough back-of-the-envelope: for 2048-token embeddings with a 70B-ish model, you're looking at a few x A100-class equivalents to hit that peak if you want sub-250ms; but if you can accept quantized 4-bit variants and batching, you can reduce GPU counts by ~2-3x. We'll provide a sizing with model variants and batching. For embedding throughput spike of ~600 RPS short windows, consider warm pools + a small reserved hot-pool sized for your steady-state and burst via reserved overflow nodes.

[16:05] Sofia Patel: We were also evaluating Dedicated vs Private on cost. Private on-prem is appealing for strict data residency, but our ops team wants minimal maintenance. What’s the operational footprint for Private vs Dedicated?
[16:20] Liam O'Connor: Private (customer-hosted control plane or on-prem package) requires more ops — you'll manage networking and some infra; Redwood provides the runtime and remote support but it's heavier. Dedicated is managed by Redwood in your cloud region with reserved tenancy and VPC peering; lower ops overhead and included maintenance. If you want minimal ops and still keep data in your VPC, Dedicated with VPC peering is usually the sweet spot.

[18:10] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Can we limit outbound egress from the inference nodes? We need to ensure no external calls leak PHI.
[18:20] Liam O'Connor: Yes — egress control enforced at the node level, and we can provide egress-blocking policies. We also have E2EE for in-transit and customer-managed keys for at-rest.

[20:45] Marcus Lin: How are model updates handled? we have a regulated workflow; updates need approvals and traceability.
[20:55] Maya Chen: Redwood supports pinned model versions and rollout policies — canary, A/B, automatic rollback, and audit trails for each deployment. We can integrate with your change approval process and provide immutable model artifacts.

[22:30] Rajesh Nair: What about retention — request logs, prompts, outputs — can we set TTL and purging rules?
[22:40] Liam O'Connor: Yes — retention policies are configurable per customer for Dedicated/Private. For Hosted, defaults are X days but enterprise packages let you set custom TTLs and deletion. We'll include retention settings in the SOW.

[25:00] Sofia Patel: Another question — our workflows do large batch embedding jobs that are cost-sensitive and can run overnight. Can we reserve capacity just for daytime low-latency chat and let batch jobs run on cheaper compute?
[25:14] Liam O'Connor: Absolutely — you can carve out dedicated pools for different workloads: a hot-pool for chat low latency and a warm/low-cost pool for batch embeddings. Redwood Optimize can suggest scheduling and quantization to lower unit costs for batch windows.

[28:50] Marcus Lin: Benchmarks — what do you need from us to run a meaningful perf test?
[28:58] Liam O'Connor: Best is a 72-hour trace with timestamps and payload sizes, plus a sample prompt set for chat and embedding payloads. Also tell us peak RPS windows and SLA targets. We'll run both steady-state and spike injections and show p50/p95/p99 and cost/unit.

[31:05] Sofia Patel: We can share a scrubbed trace. We'll need an NDA addendum for some of the test artifacts but that's fine.

[33:20] Maya Chen: Recap — Redwood will: send pricing & SOW options for a small reserved configuration + warm-pool/burst plan, include security appendix (KMS/HSM integration, audit log formats, SOC2 docs), and propose bench window. Aurum will share traffic traces and compliance questions.

[34:00] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Timeline — we aim to have a pilot in 2–3 weeks if the pricing and security are OK.

[35:45] Rajesh Nair: Quick note — we might ask for an on-site or deeper security review for Private.

[37:10] Liam O'Connor: Noted. For the pilot we'll scope a small reserved pool (1–2 GPUs warm, 4 GPUs burstable) as a starting config and tune after the bench. We'll include quantized variants to measure cost/latency tradeoffs.

[39:00] Maya Chen: Ok folks — thanks, we'll follow up with the doc packet. Any last questions?
[39:08] Sofia Patel: none, thanks.
[39:10] Marcus Lin: good, thanks.
[39:12] Rajesh Nair: Thank you.

[41:00] Maya Chen: Great, meeting ended.

Notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions (eg. "KV cash" for KV cache, "SAML" sometimes as "sam el"). Fireflies auto-summary may omit some technical nuance; please refer to the perf checklist and SOW attachments.
